sections.title: One workflow, not a random tool directory
blocks: These tools follow the same job SenderFinder handles inside Gmail and Outlook: identify the person behind a work email, confirm the likely profile, connect with a specific reason and keep the lookup cost visible. They are intentionally narrow. Generic email marketing, deliverability and profile-writing utilities would attract a different audience.

The search builder and signature parser are useful before a paid lookup. The connection note generator starts after you have confirmed the profile. The cost calculator is for deciding when manual work stops scaling and which provider-key combination fits the volume.

sections.title: The input stays in the browser
blocks: The tools do not send form input to SenderFinder and do not load an AI model, analytics script or third-party widget. A search term leaves the page only when you explicitly open a Google, Bing or LinkedIn search link. Do not paste confidential message content into any online tool; the signature parser is designed for the short signature block, not an entire sensitive thread.

The browser extension is separate. When you configure a provider key, professional lookup fields go directly from the extension to that provider. Read the privacy statement before enabling paid lookups.

sections.title: When the free route is not enough
blocks: A public-web search can miss a private profile, a signature may contain no social link and a shared address may not belong to one person. SenderFinder uses a cheapest-first enrichment waterfall for the cases that remain, compares the returned name with the mail header and marks a mismatch as uncertain instead of silently presenting it as fact.
See the 50-address email-to-LinkedIn benchmark for measured hit rates and spend, then use the install guide to try the same workflow on your own inbox.

page.faqIntro: What the tools do, where their input goes and what they cannot prove.

bottomCta.title: Bring the workflow into your inbox
bottomCta.body: SenderFinder runs the signature scan and optional provider waterfall beside the email you are already reading.

faq.a: Yes. They need no account and make no paid API call. The browser extension is also free; only optional lookups made with a provider key can cost money.

faq.q: Do the tools upload email addresses or signatures?
faq.a: No. The forms are processed in the current browser tab. A generated search query goes to the named search service only after you choose to open its link.

faq.q: Can the search builder guarantee the right LinkedIn profile?
faq.a: No. It creates useful public-web and LinkedIn searches from the clues you provide. You must compare company, title and location before treating a result as the same person.

faq.q: Why is the enrichment calculator based on a benchmark?
faq.a: A provider price alone does not describe a waterfall. The model needs the chance each step answers after earlier steps miss, so SenderFinder uses conditional hit rates measured on its published 50-address run.
